successors.name: Himyarite Kingdom
successors.text: the Kingdom of Hadramawt around Shabwa and the Wadi Hadramawt, with the former Qataban lands

ledger.x: c. 700: Hadramawt at Shabwa. 'The Kingdom of Hadhramaut was established in the early 1st millennium BCE'; 'Hadhramaut and its god Sin are mentioned in the inscription of Surwah by the Makrib Sabean writer Karib'il Watar I around 700-680 BCE'. -700 is Cliopatria's first shape and the start of the first dated…

c. 675 (bridged): Hadhramaut falls under Saba. The Sabaeans page (reopened 2026-10-19): 'Karib'il conquered all surrounding neighbours, including the Awsan, Qataban, and Hadhramaut' (reign 'late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE'; the Hadhramaut page has Hadhramaut named in Karib'il's Surwah inscription 'around 700–680…
late 7th century: a share of Awsan.

c. 330: Hadhramaut becomes independent of Saba. 'Hadhramaut became independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE', then 'allied with the Minaeans and the Kingdom of Qataban'; the History of Yemen page: 'By the 3rd century BC, Qataban, Hadramout and Ma'in became independent from Saba'.…

c. 300: Himyar annexes Hadramawt. 'Qataban in c. 200 CE, and Haḍramaut c. 300 CE' and 'By 300, the Himyarite Kingdom had vanquished other political units (including the Saba, Qataban, and Hadrawat kingdoms)'. The History of Yemen page has Shammar Yahri'sh conquer Hadramout, Najran and Tihama in 275; the…
c. 300: Hadramawt ends. The Kingdom of Hadhramaut 'ceased to exist by the end of the 3rd century CE, having been annexed by the Himyarite Kingdom'. Cliopatria's row runs to 305.

wars.name: Qatabanian-Hadramawt coalition against Saba
wars.outcome: No result recorded: the Qataban page says only that at one point in the 1st century BCE Qataban formed a coalition with Hadramawt, Radman and Madhay against the Sabaeans, without details.

wars.name: Himyarite conquest of Hadramawt
wars.outcome: Himyar annexed Hadramawt, destroying Shabwa, and ended the kingdom by 300; relations had been 'tense, with both sides waging wars against each other for control of the trade routes and territory in the region'.

certainty.note: No page gives a Hadramawt border; the shape is Cliopatria's and the region the page describes (Aden to Dhofar) is wider than the kingdom.
